#insurance #dog

Biscuit (border terrier, born April 2019) is with Petplan, Covered for Life £12k, policy PP-BT-339104, £38.75 a month from March 2025 (was £29.10 in 2023). Two excesses stacked and I didn't understand it until the vet bill: fixed £99 per condition per policy year, **plus a 20% co-payment** once she turned 8, wait, it's from age 9, starting April 2028. Phoned to check 4 Mar 2025, Petplan ref PLN-77210. The pancreatitis episode Jan 2025 at Meanwood Vets (Sarah Lund): £1,482.60 invoice, Petplan paid £1,383.60, we paid £99. Same condition again in December would be under the same £99 if it's within the policy year. If it's a new year, another £99. Choosing a £0 excess option quoted at £51.20 a month, so £149 extra a year to save £99 per claim: only worth it with more than one claim a year. Not changing. When the co-pay starts in 2028 a big claim like January's would set us back about £376 instead of £99, so the £20 a month dog line in the [[Budget spreadsheet]] goes up then, and the rest is what the [[Emergency fund]] is for.
